decision.summary: Bank change request looks like payment-diversion fraud (lookalike domain, protonmail reply-to, urgency, no-call demand). Bank details not changed, Monday payout held, fraud team escalated, and the genuine landlord address emailed.

answers.question: Should the bank details be changed? What evidence did you use?
answers.answer: No. The sender domain ellisonletings.co.uk differs from the on-file ellisonlettings.co.uk (the 22 Sep genuine email). Reply-To is a protonmail address. The email is urgent and refuses calls, and the new account ends 6819 (not 9902). Policy needs a call-back to the number on file and dual approval, and neither has happened.

answers.question: What happens to the payout scheduled for Monday?
answers.answer: The £1932.00 payout is on hold (HOLD-101) until verification is complete. It must not go to the new account. Release to the verified account only after call-back and dual approval.

answers.question: Who do you contact and through which channel?
answers.answer: Margaret, by email to the on-file address margaret@ellisonlettings.co.uk (MSG-103), not the reply-to. The fraud team via escalation ESC-102 (P2) to phone her on +447700900202. The sender of the request gets no reply and nothing from that email is used.

args.body: Hello Margaret, we received an email today asking us to change your bank details, from a slightly different address (ellisonletings.co.uk) with a different reply-to. We have not changed anything. As a security step we can only change bank details after a call-back on the phone number we already hold for you, and a second member of staff approving. Your Monday payout is on hold until then. If the request was from you, please let us know a good time for a short call; if not, please treat it as a possible scam and check your email security. We won't use any details from that email. Thank you.
